types.name: Uid
code: type Uid = string
// THE FIREBASE AUTH UID — the ONLY way a person is stored, anywhere:
// assignees, access, mentions, authors, read pointers, prefs.
// ON SCREEN A PERSON IS TWO THINGS AND A PICTURE: their display name and
// their email, with their profile picture. There are no handles and
// no usernames — nothing a person has to invent, reserve, or remember.
// Both are looked up from the uid at render time, so changing either
// changes it everywhere at once.
// The reference tracker stored EMAILS as the key ('Team > a@b.com'),
// so a changed address broke every assignment. Email is shown, never stored as a key.

types.name: PrincipalId
code: type AgentId     = string   // 'ag_' + 16 [A-Za-z0-9] — newAgentId()
type PrincipalId = Uid | AgentId
type PrincipalKind = 'user' | 'agent'
type PrincipalRef  = { kind: 'user', id: Uid } | { kind: 'agent', id: AgentId }
// PHASE 2: ANYONE WHO CAN APPEAR ON A TICKET IS A PRINCIPAL — a person
// (their Firebase uid) or an agent. Both live in the SAME fields:
// board.access keys, members/{id}, assigneeUids, watcherUids, mention
// nodes, message.authorUid, activity.actor. The 'ag_' prefix is how
// they are told apart (isAgentId / principalKind), so no field grew a
// second shape and no phase-1 document needed migrating.
// AGENTS NEVER SIGN IN TO FIREBASE. They act only through a token that
// actsAs them (platform/apiKeys), so an agent id is never in readerUids,
// never in auth.uid, and the security rules never see one.
// ONE COMPONENT DRAWS EVERY PRINCIPAL: an agent shows its picture and an
// Agent badge wherever a person would appear.

types.name: BoardId
code: type BoardId = string   // generated, never shown

types.name: TicketId
code: type TicketId = string    // generated, IMMUTABLE
// NOT THE TICKET KEY. Everything that has to survive is keyed by the
// id — the thread, the activity, every #link — so nothing anywhere
// depends on 'ENG-42' being the name it was filed under.

types.name: TicketKey
code: type TicketKey = `${BoardKey}-${number}`   // 'ENG-42'
type BoardKey  = string                    // /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,5}$/
// A BOARD KEY IS CLAIMED LIKE A USERNAME: unique across the whole app,
// first come first served (boardKeys/{key}). That is what lets
// '#ENG-42' and /t/ENG-42 mean one ticket without saying whose board.

types.name: Millis
code: type Millis = number   // epoch milliseconds, UTC
// Dates the USER picks (due, start, custom date fields) are Millis
// plus an allDay flag, so a due date of '24 Sep' does not become
// '23 Sep 18:30' for somebody in another time zone.

types.name: RichText
code: interface RichText {
// A ProseMirror / TipTap JSON document — what the editor edits.
doc: { type: 'doc', content: Node[] }
// Derived on the server, never trusted from the client:
text: string          // plain text — email, WhatsApp, search, previews
mentions: Uid[]        // every mention node in doc
refs: TicketId[]       // every #ticket node in doc
// A MENTION IS { type: 'mention', attrs: { uid } } — it stores the uid
// and RENDERS the person's current display name. Rename yourself and
// every '@Priya' you were ever mentioned in now reads '@Priya Shah'.
// Hover shows the email and the picture.

types.name: BoardRole
code: type BoardRole = 'admin' | 'editor' | 'commenter' | 'viewer'
// admin      settings, invite and remove people, change roles, delete
// editor     create + edit every field, move anywhere
// commenter  read + post in threads + move within their StageGrant
// viewer     read only
// THE ONLY ROLE THERE IS. There is no app-level role, no workspace and
// no team: the board is everything. Whoever creates a board is its
// admin; everyone else is on it because they accepted an invite to it,
// with the role that invite carried.
// AGENTS: editor | commenter | viewer, NEVER admin. boardAgentSet
// refuses 'admin'; can() reads an 'admin' entry on an agent id as editor.

types.name: StageCategory
code: type StageCategory = 'backlog' | 'todo' | 'active' | 'done' | 'cancelled'
// Stages are the board's own words ('QA', 'Waiting on client'); the
// category is what the SYSTEM reads — a ticket in any 'done' stage is
// done for My Work, for deadlines, for the board's counts.

types.name: Stage
code: interface Stage {
id: string          // 7-char base36, board-local
name: string
color: string
category: StageCategory
position: number
wipLimit?: number    // kanban column warns above this
requires?: string[]  // field ids that must be set to ENTER this stage
// requires IS THE REFERENCE'S ISSUE-LOGGER RULE, made general and moved
// to the server: 'cannot close without a Solution' was checked only in
// the browser there, so any other client skipped it.

types.name: StageGrant
code: interface StageGrant {
// Kept from the reference tracker, but PER PERSON: a commenter may
// move tickets between THESE stages only (e.g. QA: In review → Done).
stages: string[]
assignedOnly?: boolean   // only tickets assigned to them

types.name: Option
code: interface Option {           // a priority, a tag, a select choice
id: string
name: string
color?: string
position: number

types.name: FieldType
code: type FieldType =
| 'text' | 'longText' | 'number' | 'currency' | 'percent'
| 'select' | 'multiSelect' | 'checkbox' | 'rating'
| 'date' | 'dateRange' | 'person' | 'people'
| 'url' | 'email' | 'phone' | 'ticketRelation'
| 'formula'     // phase 3 — computed on the server, read-only

types.name: FieldDef
code: interface FieldDef {
id: string              // 'f_' + 6 chars; the key in Ticket.fields
name: string
type: FieldType
options?: Option[]       // select, multiSelect
config?: {
currency?: string       // 'INR'
precision?: number
max?: number            // rating
relationBoardId?: BoardId
formula?: string
required?: boolean        // enforced by ticketCreate / ticketUpdate
showOnCard?: boolean
position: number
archived?: boolean        // hidden, values kept — never destructive

types.name: FieldValue
code: type FieldValue =
| string | number | boolean | null
| string[]                        // multiSelect option ids, people uids
| { start: Millis, end: Millis }  // dateRange
| TicketId[]                        // ticketRelation
// STORED UNDER THE FIELD'S ID, never its name, so renaming 'Client'
// to 'Customer' rewrites one FieldDef and zero tickets.

types.name: FilterNode
code: type FilterNode =
| { op: 'and' | 'or', children: FilterNode[] }
| { field: string, cmp: Cmp, value?: unknown }
// field: 'stage' | 'priority' | 'assignee' | 'tag' | 'due' | 'state'
//        | 'createdBy' | 'text' | 'linked' | `fields.${fieldId}`
type Cmp = 'is' | 'isNot' | 'in' | 'notIn' | 'contains' | 'empty'
| 'notEmpty' | 'lt' | 'gt' | 'between' | 'before' | 'after'
// value may be a token: 'me', 'today', 'thisWeek', 'overdue' — so a
// saved view 'Mine, due this week' means the same thing to everyone.

types.name: ViewType
code: type ViewType = 'kanban' | 'table' | 'calendar' | 'timeline'
// FOUR, EACH WITH A COMPONENT THAT DRAWS IT. 'list' and 'gallery' were
// named here with nothing on the Screens page to render them.

types.name: TicketState
code: type TicketState = 'active' | 'archived'
// A lifecycle ORTHOGONAL to the stage. Archived tickets are read-only
// and leave every default view; restoring is admin-only. Stage says
// where the work is, state says whether it still counts as work.
// PHASE 6: 'cancelled' is gone. Archive already means 'keep it but out
// of the way', so a third read-only state earned nothing — 'Cancel
// ticket' became 'Delete ticket' (permanent, one confirm, NO reason).
// StageCategory 'cancelled' is untouched: that is a COLUMN (a board
// may keep a "Won't do" stage), not the ticket's state.

types.name: Attachment
code: interface Attachment {
id: string
path: string        // Storage path — NEVER a download URL
name: string
mime: string
size: number
width?: number      // images, for layout before load
height?: number
thumbPath?: string  // written by onAttachmentFinalized
uploadedBy: PrincipalId   // a person, or an agent through its token

types.name: FileKind
code: type FileKind = 'image' | 'video' | 'audio' | 'markdown' | 'html' | 'pdf'
| 'text' | 'csv' | 'json' | 'code' | 'other'
// fileInfo(mime, name) → { kind, language, textual } in @tm/shared —
// ONE ANSWER to 'how do we open this', used by the preview card, the
// viewer, read_file and GET /v1/files/{id}?content=1.
// EXTENSION FIRST for the documents agents write (.md, .html): their
// mime is often text/plain or application/octet-stream.
// textual kinds (markdown, html, text, csv, json, code) are returned
// inline as text to a token; the rest as a 15-minute signed URL.
// Never stored: derived from mime + name wherever it is needed.

types.name: Via
code: type Via = 'app' | 'api' | 'mcp' | 'email' | 'whatsapp' | 'intake' | 'integration' | 'system'
// WHERE A CHANGE CAME FROM, stamped on every message and activity
// row. 'Claude moved this via MCP' and 'replied by email' are facts
// the thread shows, not guesses.

types.name: NotifyEvent
code: type NotifyEvent =
| 'assigned' | 'mentioned' | 'comment' | 'stage' | 'updated'
| 'created' | 'dueSoon' | 'overdue' | 'state' | 'invited'
// PHASE 3 (§L):
| 'question'        // someone asked a blocking question (§N: an agent, or a

// person from the composer) — to the `to` people, or the
                      // assignees and watchers; loud by default
| 'agentSilence'    // YOUR agent said it was working and stopped beating (§L3)
// Events added after phase 1 are OPTIONAL on the way into
// ChannelMatrix, so a matrix stored before them still parses and gets
// their default channels.

types.name: AgentEventType
code: type AgentEventType =
| 'assigned' | 'unassigned' | 'mentioned' | 'comment'
| 'stage' | 'updated' | 'created'
// PHASE 3 (§L1) — the outcome of a question THIS agent asked:
| 'question_answered'    // carries the answer values
| 'question_cancelled'   // cancelled or expired: stop waiting
// What an orchestrator needs to react to. No dueSoon / overdue /
// invited: agents have no deadlines of their own and are never
// invited — they are added (boardAgentSet).

types.name: Question
code: interface Question {            // PHASE 3 (§L1) — Message.question, on a 'question' message
title: string                 // 'Which database should the report use?'
body: RichText | null         // optional context, rendered like a message body
fields: QuestionField[]       // 1–10
allowComment: boolean         // adds the 'Anything else?' box
to: PrincipalId[] | null      // who should answer; null = anyone on the board who may comment
blocking: boolean             // the ticket shows '❓ Waiting for your answer'
status: 'open' | 'answered' | 'cancelled' | 'expired'
expiresAt: Millis | null      // after this the card locks as Expired
answer: {                     // null until somebody submits
values: Record<fieldId, QuestionValue>   // string | number | boolean | optionId[]
comment?: string
by: Uid                     // a PERSON: agents ask, people answer
at: Millis
} | null
cancelledAt?: Millis | null
// THE QUESTION IS THE MESSAGE. Who asked, on which ticket and when all
// come from the message it hangs on, so answering rewrites one field and
// the card locks exactly where it already sits in the thread.
// Its API id is '{ticketId}.{messageId}' (GET /v1/questions/{id}); the
// board comes from the credential, so no collection-group scan is needed.

types.name: QuestionField
code: interface QuestionField {
id: string                    // stable: the answer is keyed by it
label: string
type: 'single' | 'multi' | 'text' | 'longText' | 'number' | 'boolean' | 'date'
options?: { id, label, description? }[]   // single / multi only, 1–20
required?: boolean
default?: QuestionValue       // must itself be a legal answer
placeholder?: string          // text / longText / number
// One shape for the card's form, the REST/MCP argument and the answer
// validator — a field type nobody can render is impossible to ask.

types.name: TaskItem
code: interface TaskItem {            // PHASE 3 (§L2) — one row of a tasklist
id: string
title: string
status: 'todo' | 'doing' | 'done' | 'skipped' | 'failed'
note?: string                 // why it failed, what was skipped, where the output went
updatedAt: Millis             // kept when a replace leaves the row untouched
// 'doing' is the one with the spinner; 'failed' is red and shows its note.
// done + skipped are what the progress bar has behind it.

types.name: AgentState
code: type AgentState = 'working' | 'idle' | 'done' | 'error'
// PHASE 3 (§L3): what the ORCHESTRATOR says it is doing, in its beat.

types.name: AgentHealth
code: type AgentHealth = 'working' | 'stale' | 'idle' | 'done' | 'error' | 'none'
// PHASE 3 (§L3): what the UI SHOWS, derived from the state and the age of
// the last beat — never stored. deriveAgentHealth(status, now):
//   working, beat ≤ 75 s   🟢 'Working · Running tests (3/12)' (pulsing)
//   working, beat > 75 s   🔴 'No signal for 3 min'  — it may have died
//   idle                   🟡 'Idle · waiting for an answer'
//   done                   ⚪ 'Finished · 10:42'
//   error                  🔴 'Stopped with an error' + the message
//   no document            nothing at all
// 75 s = one missed beat plus slack, so a dot goes red by itself. The
// screen recomputes every 15 s; nobody writes 'stale' anywhere.

types.name: Channel
code: type Channel = 'inApp' | 'push' | 'email' | 'whatsapp'

types.name: BoardNotifyPref
code: interface BoardNotifyPref {
// The reference tracker's NOTIFY_PREF, minus its 'teams' mode:
//   all    — everything on the board
//   mine   — tickets I'm assigned to, created, or watch
//   muted  — only tickets I explicitly watch, and mentions
mode: 'all' | 'mine' | 'muted'
events?: NotifyEvent[]     // absent = every event
stageIds?: string[]        // 'stage' events: only into these stages
// Set by the person themselves — from the bell on the board's bar, or
// the per-board list in Account › Notifications. Nobody sets it for you.

types.name: ChannelMatrix
code: type ChannelMatrix = Record<NotifyEvent, Channel[]>
// WHICH CHANNELS AN EVENT USES — chosen by EACH PERSON in Account ›
// Notifications, and by nobody else. No board and no admin can turn a
// channel on for you or off for you.
// Defaults for a new account:
//   mentioned, assigned, invited  → inApp, push, email
//   dueSoon, overdue              → inApp, push, email
//   everything else               → inApp
// 'whatsapp' is offered only once a number is linked and opted in,
// and is off for every event until the person ticks it.

schema.name: users
rules: allow get:    signedIn()
allow list:   never
allow write:  never   // profileUpdate — a name or picture change fans out to every board
// ANY SIGNED-IN PERSON MAY GET A PROFILE BY UID, because a card showing
// an avatar needs one — but not LIST them. Listing people is what a
// board's members/ is for, and only for that board.
schema: interface User {
name: string              // DISPLAY NAME — shown everywhere, editable, not unique
email: string             // from Auth, verified — shown beside the name, changed only via Auth
avatarPath: string | null // PROFILE PICTURE: users/{uid}/avatar/{millis}.webp, 256px
timezone: string          // 'Asia/Kolkata' — digests, quiet hours, due dates
locale: string
theme: 'system' | 'light' | 'dark'
whatsapp: { number: string, verifiedAt: Millis, optIn: boolean } | null
// EVERY NOTIFICATION CHOICE LIVES HERE, on the person — see ChannelMatrix.
notify: {
channels: ChannelMatrix
quietHours: { start: '22:00', end: '08:00' } | null
digest: 'off' | 'hourly' | 'daily'
dueSoonLeadMinutes: number   // 'remind me this long before a due date' — default 1440
commitmentReminders: boolean
createdAt: Millis
deletedAt: Millis | null     // soft delete, see accountDelete

schema.name: agents
rules: allow read:  auth.uid == resource.data.ownerUid
allow write: never   // agentCreate, agentUpdate, agentArchive
// AN AGENT PROFILE IS PRIVATE TO THE PERSON WHO MADE IT. Nobody else
// reads it — not even an admin of a board it is on. What a board sees
// is the copy in members/{agentId}: name, picture, description, role.
// The system prompt never leaves this document except to the agent's
// OWN tokens (GET /v1/me, MCP whoami).
// Top-level, not under users/{uid}, because the id alone must resolve
// it: a token, a member row and the inbox all carry just the agentId.
schema: interface Agent {
ownerUid: Uid                 // the person who made it; only they see or change it
name: string                  // 1–60
avatarPath: string | null     // users/{ownerUid}/agents/{agentId}/avatar/{millis}.webp
icon?: string | null          // a prebuilt icon id (shared AGENT_ICON_IDS: 'claude', 'gemini', 'bot', …);
// shown on the agent's colour when there is no picture: avatarPath > icon > initials
systemPrompt: string          // Markdown, ≤ 50 000 chars
description: string | null    // one line (≤ 200), shown in pickers
createdAt: Millis
updatedAt: Millis
archivedAt: Millis | null     // archived: off every board, its tokens revoked
// AN AGENT PROFILE IS { name, picture, system prompt } AND NOTHING
// ELSE. Which model runs it, where, and with which tools is the
// orchestrator's business; this app only needs to know who is
// speaking and what to hand the orchestrator when it asks.
// QUERY: where(ownerUid == me).orderBy(updatedAt, desc) — the Agents page.
// 50 agents per person.

schema.name: devices
rules: allow read, delete: auth.uid == uid
allow create, update: auth.uid == uid && validDevice()
// The one collection a client writes directly: registering this
// browser for push is a fact about the browser, holds no invariant
// across documents, and must work on the first page load.
schema: interface Device {
fcmToken: string
kind: 'web' | 'ios' | 'android'
userAgent: string
lastSeenAt: Millis
// Tokens FCM reports as unregistered are deleted by the push sender.

schema.name: inbox
rules: allow read:   auth.uid == uid
allow update: auth.uid == uid && onlyChanges(['readAt', 'archivedAt', 'snoozedUntil'])
allow create, delete: never
// THE IN-APP CHANNEL. The bell is a realtime listener on
// where(archivedAt == null).orderBy(createdAt, desc).limit(50).
schema: interface InboxItem {
event: NotifyEvent
boardId: BoardId
ticketId: TicketId | null      // null for 'invited'
ticketKey: TicketKey | null     // denormalised for rendering
ticketTitle: string | null
inviteId: string | null         // 'invited': Accept / Decline right in the row
actor: Uid | null     // null for dueSoon / overdue
via: Via
summary: string       // 'moved to QA', 'mentioned you: …'
messageId?: string    // deep link into the thread
groupKey: string      // `${ticketId}:${event}` — collapses 5 comments into one row
count: number         // how many were collapsed
createdAt: Millis
readAt: Millis | null
archivedAt: Millis | null
snoozedUntil: Millis | null

schema.name: agentInbox
rules: allow read:  auth.uid == get(/agents/$(agentId)).data.ownerUid
allow write: never   // notify() writes; agentInboxAck acks
// THE AGENT'S EVENT FEED — what users/{uid}/inbox is for a person.
// Agents get no push, email or WhatsApp; an orchestrator polls this
// (GET /v1/events), streams it (GET /v1/events/stream, SSE) or asks
// for it over MCP (get_events), and acks what it handled.
// eventId = agentEventId(createdAt, suffix): base36 millis padded to
// 9 chars + '_' + suffix, so ids SORT BY TIME and the id IS the
// cursor. 'Everything after X' is one orderBy(__name__) query, and
// ack { upTo } is one range.
schema: interface AgentInboxEvent {
type: AgentEventType
boardId: BoardId
ticketId: TicketId
ticketKey: TicketKey          // denormalised: 'ENG-42' at the time of the event
messageId?: string | null     // comment / mentioned: the message to read
actor: PrincipalId | null     // a person or ANOTHER agent; null = the system
summary: string               // 'Priya assigned you ENG-42', 'moved to QA'
createdAt: Millis
question?: {                  // PHASE 3: question_answered / _cancelled
id, title, status, values?, comment?, answeredBy?
}                             // the values are IN the event — no second call
ackedAt: Millis | null        // REST POST /v1/events/ack, MCP ack_events
// WHO GETS ONE: an agent assigned to or watching the ticket, and any
// agent a message mentions. THE AGENT'S OWN ACTIONS NEVER CREATE AN
// EVENT FOR ITSELF — an orchestrator that posts a comment must not
// wake up to its own comment.
// NOT COLLAPSED, unlike a person's inbox. A person reads a row; a
// program handles each event, and two comments are two things to do.
// Unacked events are kept; acked ones are TTL-deleted 30 days after
// ackedAt (Firestore TTL policy on a derived expireAt).

schema.name: reads
rules: allow read: auth.uid == uid
allow write: auth.uid == uid && onlyChanges(['readAt', 'boardId'])
// UNREAD = ticket.lastMessageAt > reads/{ticketId}.readAt. The reference
// tracker kept a conv_log array ON the ticket and a pointer per email
// inside it — every read was a write to the most contended document
// on the board. A per-user doc makes 'mark read' touch nothing shared.
schema: interface Read { boardId: BoardId, readAt: Millis }

schema.name: invites
rules: allow get, list: resource.data.email == auth.token.email && auth.token.email_verified
|| boardRole(resource.data.boardId) == 'admin'
allow write: never
// TOP-LEVEL, NOT UNDER THE BOARD, because the question it answers is
// 'what have I been invited to' — where(email == mine), across boards —
// and the invitee cannot read the board until they accept.
// The token in the email link is never stored, only its SHA-256.
schema: interface Invite {
boardId: BoardId
boardName: string         // the invitee can't read the board yet
boardKey: BoardKey
email: string             // lower-cased
role: BoardRole
invitedBy: Uid
invitedByName: string
message: string | null
tokenHash: string
status: 'pending' | 'accepted' | 'declined' | 'revoked' | 'expired'
expiresAt: Millis          // 14 days
createdAt: Millis

schema.name: boardKeys
rules: allow get: signedIn()   // 'is ENG free?' while typing a new board's key
allow list, write: never
// Created by boardCreate in the same transaction as the board; a second
// create of the same id fails, which is the uniqueness.
schema: interface BoardKeyClaim { boardId: BoardId, claimedAt: Millis }

schema.name: boards
rules: allow get:  canRead(boardId)
allow list: signedIn()   // query MUST be where(readerUids array-contains auth.uid)
allow write: never
function canRead(b)   { auth.uid in get(/boards/$(b)).data.readerUids }
function boardRole(b) { get(/boards/$(b)).data.access[auth.uid] }
// A BOARD IS PRIVATE TO ITS PEOPLE. There is nothing above it: no
// workspace, no directory, no 'visible to everyone'. You see a board
// because you created it or accepted an invite to it.
// readerUids is the keys of access, derived — a list QUERY can only be
// proven with array-contains, never with 'is a key of this map'.
schema: interface Board {
name: string
key: BoardKey              // 'ENG' — claimed in boardKeys/{key}, app-wide
nextNumber: number         // allocateKey increments in a transaction
color: string
icon: string
description: RichText | null
access:     Record<PrincipalId, BoardRole>   // THE authority; mirrored in members/ — people AND agents
stageGrants: Record<PrincipalId, StageGrant>   // per principal, commenters only
readerUids: Uid[]          // derived: every PERSON with any role — never an agent
editorUids: Uid[]          // derived: editor + admin people — never an agent
stages: Stage[]
priorities: Option[]
tags: Option[]
fields: FieldDef[]
defaultViewId: string
settings: {
allowDelete: boolean            // hard delete opt-in (reference)
emailReplies: boolean           // replying to a mail posts a comment
autoArchiveDoneAfterDays: number | null
counts: { active: number, done: number, overdue: number }   // overdue kept true by deadlineSweep, not by writes
archivedAt: Millis | null    // boardArchive: read-only, hidden from the sidebar, restorable
createdBy: Uid
createdAt: Millis
// NOTIFICATION PREFS ARE NOT HERE. The reference kept everyone's prefs in
// one column on the board and stripped it in the route; a Firestore
// rule cannot hide one key of a map, so they live in prefs/{uid}.

schema.name: members
rules: allow read:  canRead(boardId)
allow write: never   // inviteAccept, boardAccessSet, boardAgentSet
// THE BOARD'S PEOPLE AND AGENTS: who is on it, with what role, and
// how to show them. It is the @mention directory for this board's
// composer and the assignee picker — you can only assign someone
// (or some agent) that is here.
// board.access (below) is the AUTHORITY the rules read; this is the
// same fact denormalised for display, written in the same transaction.
schema: interface BoardMember {
kind: PrincipalKind         // 'user' | 'agent' — absent on phase-1 docs, read as 'user'
uid: PrincipalId            // also the doc id; a field so collectionGroup can find it
role: BoardRole             // agents: never 'admin'
stageGrant: StageGrant | null   // commenters only
// copied so the pickers are one query; kept in step by profileUpdate
// (people) and agentUpdate (agents):
name: string
email: string               // '' for agents
avatarPath: string | null   // users/{uid}/avatar/… or users/{ownerUid}/agents/{agentId}/avatar/…
icon?: string | null        // agents: the prebuilt icon id, copied like avatarPath
invitedBy: Uid | null       // null for the board's creator, and for agents
joinedAt: Millis
// agents only:
ownerUid?: Uid              // the person who owns the agent profile
addedBy?: Uid               // the board admin (always the owner) who added it
description?: string | null // its one line, shown under the name in pickers
// THE PICKER MATCHES NAME OR EMAIL. Two 'Priya's are told apart by the
// email under each name and by the picture — which is what a handle
// was for, without anyone having to choose one. An agent is told apart
// by its badge and its description.
// AN AGENT IS ADDED, NOT INVITED. It has no inbox to accept from, and
// its owner already decided — boardAgentSet writes this row directly.

schema.name: prefs
rules: allow read:  auth.uid == uid
allow write: never   // boardPrefSet — your own, only
// ONE DOCUMENT PER PERSON PER BOARD, because Firestore cannot hide
// one key of a map. The reference kept everyone's prefs in one column
// and let the board owner set them for everybody; here nobody can set
// anyone else's.
schema: interface BoardPref extends BoardNotifyPref {
watching: TicketId[]     // 'subscribed' in the reference — always notify
starred: boolean       // pinned in the sidebar
lastViewId: string

schema.name: views
rules: allow read: canRead(boardId)
&& (resource.data.scope == 'shared' || resource.data.ownerUid == auth.uid)
allow write: never   // viewSave
// PERSONAL AND SHARED VIEWS in one collection. A personal view is a
// saved filter nobody else sees; promoting it to shared needs editor.
schema: interface View {
name: string
type: ViewType
scope: 'shared' | 'personal'
ownerUid: Uid
position: number
filter: FilterNode | null
sort: { field: string, dir: 'asc' | 'desc' }[]
groupBy: string | null       // 'stage' | 'priority' | 'assignee' | `fields.${id}`
subGroupBy: string | null    // swimlanes
columns: { field: string, width: number, hidden?: boolean }[]  // table
dateField: string | null     // calendar / timeline: 'due' | `fields.${id}`
endDateField: string | null  // timeline bar end
cardFields: string[]         // what a kanban card shows
includeStates: TicketState[]   // default ['active']

schema.name: tickets
rules: allow read: canRead(boardId)
allow write: never
// match /{path=**}/tickets/{ticketId}  — the collection-group rule
allow read: auth.uid in resource.data.assigneeUids

|| auth.uid in resource.data.watcherUids
        || auth.uid == resource.data.createdBy
// TWO READ PATHS, ONE PER SCREEN. The board screen queries one
// board's subcollection, where canRead needs one get(). My Work is a
// collection-group query where(assigneeUids array-contains me), and
// its rule is provable from the query itself — no get() at all.
// ALL WRITES GO THROUGH THE COMMAND LAYER, because nearly every one
// has a second document to keep true: the key counter, the activity
// row, the other ticket's link, the notification fan-out, the search
// index. See the architecture page, 'One command layer'.
schema: interface Ticket {
key: TicketKey               // 'ENG-42' — allocated once, never reissued
number: number
title: string
description: RichText | null
stageId: string
stageCategory: StageCategory // denormalised so My Work can query 'not done'
priorityId: string | null
tagIds: string[]
state: TicketState
rank: string                 // fractional index — order inside a column
assigneeUids: PrincipalId[]  // people AND agents, directly — any member with a role on this board
watcherUids: PrincipalId[]   // creator + assignees + anyone who opted in
reporter: { uid: Uid | null, name: string, email?: string }  // intake has no uid
startAt: Millis | null
dueAt: Millis | null
dueAllDay: boolean
commitments: Record<Uid, Millis>   // reference 'pickup dates': per person
estimate: number | null            // points or hours, board decides
fields: Record<string, FieldValue> // FieldDef.id → value
// HOW TICKETS RELATE — there are no subtasks. A big piece of work is a
// ticket whose description or thread #references the smaller ones, or
// that 'relates' / 'blocks' them. References and links are enough.
refs: TicketId[]             // #tickets this one mentions (description + messages)
referencedBy: TicketId[]     // tickets that #mention THIS one — the backlink, written by the
// same transaction, so a reference is visible from both ends
links: { type: 'blocks' | 'blockedBy' | 'relates' | 'duplicates', ticketId: TicketId }[]
// written on BOTH tickets by ticketUpdate (blocks ↔ blockedBy)
counts: { messages: number, files: number, pinned: number }
lastMessageAt: Millis | null
lastActivityAt: Millis
// PHASE 3 (§L1 · §L2) — the two CARD SUMMARIES, rolled up by the commands
// that change a question or a task list, so a board of 300 cards reads both
// from the snapshot it already has instead of a second query per card.
waitingOn?: {                   // the oldest OPEN BLOCKING question, or null
count, messageId, title, to: PrincipalId[] | null, askedBy, askedAt, expiresAt
} | null
tasklistProgress?: { done: number, total: number } | null   // the '4/7' chip
dueNotified: Record<Uid, { soon?: Millis, overdue?: Millis }>
// PER PERSON: each has their own lead time, so one
// person's reminder must not silence another's
createdBy: PrincipalId       // an agent's token creates tickets as the agent
createdVia: Via
createdAt: Millis
updatedAt: Millis
completedAt: Millis | null   // set when stageCategory becomes 'done'
// INDEXES (firestore.indexes.json):
//   tickets: state ASC, stageId ASC, rank ASC              — kanban columns
//   tickets: state ASC, dueAt ASC                          — calendar
//   group tickets: assigneeUids CONTAINS, stageCategory, dueAt  — My Work
//   group tickets: state, dueAt                            — deadlineSweep

schema.name: messages
rules: allow read: canRead(boardId)
allow write: never
// THE THREAD. A realtime listener, newest 50, older on scroll.
// Pinned messages are a second listener: where(pinnedAt != null).
schema: interface Message {

kind: 'comment' | 'system' | 'question'   // system: 'Priya moved this to QA'
                                 // question: PHASE 3 — a form card; the payload is in `question`
body: RichText
markdown?: string | null       // PHASE 2: the Markdown SOURCE when posted as Markdown (REST
// body_markdown, MCP post_message). The thread renders it as
// GitHub-flavoured Markdown — tables, images, highlighted code,
// more than RichText holds. body stays the derived doc for text,
// mentions, refs and search. Cleared by an edit in the app editor.
authorUid: PrincipalId | null   // a person or an agent; null when via email/intake from an outsider
authorName: string
via: Via
viaToken?: string | null        // PHASE 2: the token's name — 'Builder (agent) via token orch-eng-builder'
replyTo: string | null          // quoted message id — one level, not nested threads
attachments: Attachment[]
reactions: Record<string, PrincipalId[]>   // '👍' → principals
pinnedAt: Millis | null
pinnedBy: PrincipalId | null
editedAt: Millis | null
deletedAt: Millis | null        // tombstone: 'This message was deleted'
createdAt: Millis
question?: Question | null      // PHASE 3 (§L1): present exactly when kind is 'question'.
// questionAnswer / questionCancel rewrite this ONE field, so
// the card locks where it already sits in the thread.
// WHY NOT NESTED REPLIES: a ticket thread is already the reply to
// one thing. Quote-reply keeps context without a second tree to
// paginate, and the reference tracker never needed one.

schema.name: activity
rules: allow read: canRead(boardId)
allow write: never
schema: interface Activity {
action: 'create' | 'update' | 'state' | 'link' | 'referenced'
changes: Record<string, { from: unknown, to: unknown }>  // raw ids, UI resolves names
actor: PrincipalId | null   // a person or an agent
via: Via
viaToken?: string | null    // PHASE 2: the token's name when a token made the change
viaGrant?: string[]     // reference: which StageGrant authorised a limited move
createdAt: Millis
// Written in the SAME transaction as the change it describes — the
// reference logged best-effort after the fact, so a failed log was
// a change with no history.

schema.name: files
rules: allow read: canRead(boardId)
allow write: never
// EVERY FILE ON A TICKET, IN ONE PLACE — the drawer's Files tab. Files
// arrive with a message, with the description, or with ticketCreate;
// without this list the tab would have to page through the whole
// thread to find them, and the description's files were stored nowhere.
// AGENTS UPLOAD FIRST, POST SECOND. An orchestrator writes plan.md or
// report.html with upload_file, gets a fileId, and names it in
// post_message — so a file can exist here before any message does.
// The card, the viewer and /f/{boardKey}/{ticketKey}/{fileId} all
// start from this row (see FileKind).
schema: interface TicketFile extends Attachment {
source: 'description' | 'message' | 'upload'
// 'upload' (phase 2): put on the ticket by POST /v1/tickets/{KEY}/files
// or MCP upload_file and not yet posted; messagePost's fileIds then
// attaches it (source → 'message', messageId set)
messageId: string | null    // jump to where it was posted
createdAt: Millis
deletedAt: Millis | null    // its message was deleted

schema.name: tasklists
rules: allow read:  canRead(boardId)
allow write: never   // tasklistSet / tasklistItemUpdate / tasklistDelete
// PHASE 3 (§L2) / PHASE 5 (§N2) — A PLAN, ticked off as the work happens:

// an agent's, or a person's, on the same ticket and in the same pane.
// Its OWN document, not a field on the ticket: ticking an item must
// not rewrite the ticket, or every beat of progress would retrigger
// search indexing, the activity feed and every open listener.
schema: interface Tasklist {
title: string                  // 'Plan: add CSV export'
owner: PrincipalId             // usually the agent; a person's list is theirs
items: TaskItem[]              // ≤ 100
position: number               // order among the lists on a ticket
createdAt: Millis
updatedAt: Millis
closedAt: Millis | null        // the plan was declared finished
// WHO MAY CHANGE ONE: the owner (an agent through its token, a person

// signed in), and board editors and admins. Commenters and viewers
// read it. The browser and an agent call the same three commands.
// THE THREAD ONLY HEARS TWICE: a system line when the list is created
// and one when it is finished. Ticking says nothing, or the thread
// would be unreadable.
// The ticket carries the roll-up (tickets.tasklistProgress) so a board
// card shows '4/7' without reading this collection.

schema.name: agentStatus
rules: allow read:  canRead(boardId)
allow write: never   // agentHeartbeat writes; agentSilenceSweep stamps
// PHASE 3 (§L3) — IS THE AGENT ALIVE?
// The doc id is the beat STREAM: one agent on one ticket, or
// '{agentId}___' for an agent-level beat about no ticket.
// THE BOARD LISTENS HERE ONCE and every card, the drawer header,
// People & roles and the Agents page read from that one snapshot.
schema: interface AgentStatus {
agentId: AgentId
ticketId: TicketId | null      // null = an agent-level beat
state: AgentState              // what the orchestrator says it is doing
message: string | null         // 'Running tests (3/12)' — ≤ 200 chars
progress: number | null        // 0–1
lastBeatAt: Millis             // every minute while it works
startedAt: Millis              // the first beat of this run
endedAt: Millis | null         // a 'done' / 'error' beat; cleared when work restarts
silenceNotifiedAt?: Millis | null   // the owner has been told about THIS silence
// WHY NOT ON THE TICKET: a beat a minute per agent would rewrite the
// ticket a minute, retriggering indexing and every listener on it.
// These documents are small, and nothing but the dot reads them.
// What is SHOWN is AgentHealth, derived from state + age of lastBeatAt.

schema.name: keys
rules: allow get: signedIn()
allow list, write: never
// '#ENG-42' → the ticket it names. Reading this reveals only ids;
// reading the ticket itself still needs a role on its board.
// A DELETED ticket's key is KEPT (deleted: true) and never reissued, so
// an old link or an old email says 'this is gone' rather than landing
// on somebody else's work.
schema: interface KeyIndex {
ticketId: TicketId
boardId: BoardId
current: TicketKey    // the key itself — equal to the doc id
deleted?: boolean     // the ticket was deleted; the key stays taken

schema.name: attachments
rules: allow read:   canReadBoard(boardId)  // firestore.get() from storage rules
allow create: canWriteBoard(boardId)
&& request.resource.size < 50 * 1024 * 1024
allow update, delete: never
// UPLOAD DIRECT, ATTACH THROUGH A COMMAND. The browser uploads to
// Storage with progress; then messagePost / ticketUpdate names the
// path, and the command checks the object exists and is under this
// ticket's prefix. An uploaded file nobody attached is swept after 24h.
// match /users/{uid}/avatar/{file}
//   allow read:  signedIn()
//   allow write: auth.uid == uid && image/* && size < 5 MB
// match /users/{uid}/agents/{agentId}/avatar/{file}   (phase 2)
//   allow read:  signedIn()
//   allow write: auth.uid == uid && image/* && size < 5 MB
// Files a TOKEN uploads (REST / MCP, ≤ 25 MB) are written by the server
// under the same ticket prefix. Browsers read every file through a
// short-lived download URL the rules only issue to people on the board.
schema: // thumbnails: …/{attachmentId}/thumb_400.webp  (onAttachmentFinalized)
// avatars:    users/{uid}/avatar/{millis}.webp  (profile picture; owner-only write, 5 MB, image/*)
// exports:    exports/{uid}/{jobId}.zip  (accountExport, signed URL, 7 days)
// agent pictures: users/{ownerUid}/agents/{agentId}/avatar/{millis}.webp  (agentCreate / agentUpdate)

schema.name: presence
rules: .read:  root.child('boardReaders').child($boardId).child(auth.uid).exists()
.write: auth.uid == $uid
// boardReaders/{boardId}/{uid} is a mirror of readerUids, written by
// the same functions — RTDB rules cannot read Firestore.
// RTDB, NOT FIRESTORE, because onDisconnect() exists here.
schema: interface Presence {
state: 'online' | 'away'
viewing: TicketId | null   // 'Priya is looking at this' avatars in the drawer
lastChanged: ServerValue.TIMESTAMP

schema.name: typing
rules: .read:  boardReaders/{boardId} mirror, as presence
.write: auth.uid == $uid
schema: // { at: TIMESTAMP } — shown for 5s, removed onDisconnect

schema.name: tickets index
rules: // NO DIRECT ACCESS WITHOUT A SCOPED KEY. searchKey mints a
// Typesense scoped key embedding filter_by: boardId:[…readable…],
// valid for 1h; the browser searches with it directly.
// WHY A SEARCH ENGINE AT ALL: Firestore has no full-text and no
// prefix-on-any-word. The '#' picker ('#login' → ENG-42 Fix login
// redirect) and the ⌘K palette both need exactly that.
schema: interface TicketDoc {
id: TicketId
boardId: BoardId
key: TicketKey        // infix-searchable: '42' finds ENG-42
title: string
text: string          // description + last 20 messages, plain
stageCategory: StageCategory
assigneeUids: Uid[]
state: TicketState
updatedAt: number
// Synced by onTicketWritten. Messages' text folded in by onMessageWritten.
